previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with a history of endometriosis, bipolar disorder, and chronic pelvic pain was admitted for acute on chronic left pelvic pain, consistent with prior flares. She presented with severe pain and nausea, unable to tolerate oral intake. Initial labs showed elevated lactate that improved with supportive care, and no signs of infection. Urine tests were negative for chlamydia and gonorrhea. She was restarted on her home pain regimen, including gabapentin, ibuprofen, and tramadol, and received IV fluids for dehydration. Her hemoglobin declined to 9.9 g/dL, reflecting ongoing anemia likely due to menorrhagia, and outpatient colonoscopy was scheduled to evaluate for rectal endometriosis. Lithium level was therapeutic, and subclinical hypothyroidism was noted but not treated. She improved clinically, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with follow-up plans in gynecology and for surgical evaluation.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ y/o female with bipolar disorder, endometriosis s/p 
laparoscopic excision x2, presenting with LLQ pain typical of 
prior exacerbations of endometrial pain without acute abdomen. 
She was incidentally found to have RLL PNA during this 
hospitalization. She was started on Depo for presumed recurrent 
endometriosis and abx for RLL PNA, greatly improved at time of 
discharge.

#LLQ Abdominal Pain/Nausea:
Consulted Ob/Gyn since symptoms very similar to prior admissions 
for endometriosis. Given CT abdomen/pelvis results and 
transvaginal ultrasound (and pelvic exam) indicative of no acute 
abdominal or pelvic pathology, it was felt that the pain was 
most likely an exacerbation of her chronic endometriosis, 
possibly in the setting of recent change in OCPs. Patient was 
started on Depo Provera on ___ in the hospital with a 
plan to follow up within 2 weeks with Ob/Gyn. Pain control was 
provided for the abdominal discomfort, and in addition serial 
abdominal exams indicated no acute abdomen during 
hospitalization. Pain gradually subsided and was controlled with 
medications at the time of discharge.

#RLL PNA
During evaluation of a fever, she was found to have RLL PNA 
(likely HCAP given >48 hours of hospitalization), though she 
denied SOB or cough. PICC placed in left arm on ___ due 
to lack of venous access. Patient placed on Vanc/Cefepime. 
Initially also on Flagyl given concern for abscess 
___ given recent laparoscopy, but later discontinued 
as she was clinically very ___. In addition to 
antibiotics treatment, patient was encouraged to take in PO 
fluids, and was bolused normal saline as needed. Oxygen 
saturation was maintained greater than 90% via supplemental O2. 
Prior to discharge the PICC line was discontinued and patient 
received one dose of Levofloxacin 750mg PO, with discontinuation 
of her IV abx. She was informed of warning signs to watch for 
including fever/chills/shortness of breath, and if experiencing 
any of these asked to see urgent care. Surveillance blood 
cultures were NGTD on discharge from the hospital, and there 
were no signs of bacteremia/sepsis. Symptoms of mylagias/malaise 
resolved by the time of discharge, with no fever in preceding 24 
hours of discharge.

You came to ___ with abdominal 
pain, nausea and vomiting that was found to be most likely 
related to an exacerbation of your chronic endometriosis pain. 
During your hospitalization you also developed a pneumonia. You 
were treated with IV antibiotics via a ___ line and 
transitioned to oral antibiotics. Your pain gradually improved

take QT prolonging agents such as Trazodone or Thorazine while 
undergoing your antibiotic course. Wait at least a full 48 hours 
after your final dose of antibiotics to resume medications such
